title: 3D market graph payload
description: The normalized render grid emitted by dca_market_graph.build_payload() and consumed by both viz/market_graph.js and analysis/market-graph-3d/render_market_graph.py. Every price channel is a percent move against the bar's prior close divided by scales.pct_per_unit; the volume channel is already mapped to [0, 1]. A null in any series array means the ticker did not trade that session -- renderers must skip that frame rather than substituting zero, which would draw a fabricated flat day.

schema_version.description: Bumped when a field changes meaning. The viewer refuses to render an unrecognised version rather than misreading the arrays.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the build.

source.description: Which loader produced the bars (csv, archive, intraday, provider).

whole_market.description: True when the volume channel is relative volume and a __MARKET__ centroid series is appended.

dates.description: The shared session axis, ascending. Every series array is indexed by position in this list. Entries are YYYY-MM-DD for daily sources, and 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MMZ' when any bar carries a time (the intraday and run-dir sources legitimately produce several frames per calendar day) -- meta.intraday says which. The trailing Z is literal: intraday frames are UTC, not the Eastern trading clock used elsewhere in this repo.

yl.description: Low, as normalized move vs prior close.

yh.description: High, as normalized move vs prior close.

zo.description: Open, as normalized move vs prior close.

zc.description: Close, as normalized move vs prior close.

pct_per_unit.description: Multiply any yl/yh/zo/zc value by this to recover the real fractional move vs prior close.

percentile.description: Percentile of absolute moves used to set pct_per_unit.

source.description: How the ticker axis was ordered. 'returns' is the built-in stdlib return-correlation seriation; 'ml-forecaster' is the richer behavioral export; 'none' means unordered. Surfaced in the viewer so a chart never silently uses the weaker grouping.

intraday.description: True when the frame axis carries times as well as dates.

channel.description: One value per entry in `dates`; null where the ticker did not trade.
